main_text.p: à concione & quæ cum eâ cohærebant, ad judicia eundum.

Iudicia Athenis varia fuerunt, sed præ-cipua quatuor; quæ pro conciliis merito habere possumus, juri dicundo destinata, Areopagiticum, Ephetarum, Heliasticum, & Διαιτητῶν[?] sive arbitrorum.[illegible, ~4 letters] In his actiones forenses discepta-[illegible, ~5 letters]bantur, quas Græci δίκας vocant: unde, vel λόγῳ δὲ δικαζῶν[?] δικαστήρια[?], id est, confessus aut tribunalia judicum porrò nuncupantur. Αἰκαὶ autem, vel actiones, erant duplicis generis; publicæ scilicet & privatæ. Publicas κοινὰς[?] privatas proprie δίκας appel-[illegible, ~3 letters]labant. Publicæ cuivis civi erant concessæ: privatæ læsis tantum, aut iis quorum privatim intererat. Vtriusque generis variæ erant species. Καταγραφῶν erant γραφὴ, Φάσις, ἐνδείξις, ἀπαγωγὴ, ἀφήγησις, ἀνδραποδισμία[?], εἰσαγ-[illegible, ~4 letters]λία: quarum γραφὴ latissimè patebat ad crimina multa pertinens. Αἰκαὶ actiones erant de convitiis, verberatio-[illegible, ~3 letters]ne, vi illatâ, ebrietate, malâ tractatione, furto & similibus. In Καληγορίαις[?] cui-[illegible, ~3 letters]libet

page.notes: Right margin: about ten or more fragments of marginal notes are visible, mostly Greek abbreviations and a few Latin words. They are cut off by the edge of the scan and at this resolution cannot be read; each group is marked as illegible, and the placement within the paragraph is approximate. Greek words marked [?] are doubtful readings: the scan is blurred and the Greek letters are not fully legible (notably the title of the arbitrators, the phrase after "unde", "κοινὰς", "ἀνδραποδισμία" and the name beginning "Καληγορ-"). The Greek hyphenated word "εἰσαγ-/λία" is probably εἰσαγγελία. "cui-/libet" is printed with a line-end hyphen and is transcribed as printed. Printing errors left as printed: "pracipua" (for praecipua), "Αἰκαὶ" and "Αἰκας" (probably Αἰκαί/δίκαι variants). Cut-off edge at the right of the scan.
